title: How fast did Britain get richer?
hook: Income per person in England doubled in 430 years. What did Britain's next 318 years do?

knows: that people are richer now than in the past
doesNotKnow: that for centuries income per person barely moved
that nearly all the growth came in the last 300 years

misconception: Living standards rose slowly and steadily through history.
objective: The learner can say that England's income per person only about doubled in the 430 years to 1700 (about 0.16% a year) but grew about 16-fold in the 318 years after (about 0.87% a year, doubling about every 80 years), and that the series before 1700 is a modern reconstruction.

claims.text: Growth of 0.16% a year is invisible in a lifetime, which is why, on the linear scale, most of history looks flat (reveal: 'On the linear scale most of history looks flat').

claims.text: From 1700 to 2018 the record sits below the dashed steady 0.87%-a-year line because 0.87% is the span's average: growth was slower before 1850 (×1.80, 0.39% a year, 1700-1850) and faster after (×8.79, 1.30% a year, 1850-2018) (reveal: 'on the log scale the record sags below the dashed 0.87% average, as growth was slower before 1850 and faster after').

(4332/2412)^(1/150) − 1 = 0.39%; (38058/4332)^(1/168) − 1 = 1.30%. Against the model 2,412 × 1.00871^(y − 1700), the series is below it in 304 of the 317 years 1701-2017; it is above it only in 5 years just after 1700 (1701, 1702, 1704, 1705, 1708, by 2-11%) and in 8 years from 2002 (2002-2008 and 2017) (builder's node script, re-run 2026-10-15). The split year 1850 is the builder's choice; other splits show the same speed-up (1700-1800 0.33%, 1800-1900 0.82%, 1900-2018 1.38% a year).

recall.question: One economy grows 0.2% a year for 300 years, another 2% a year for 30 years. Which grows more in total?
recall.why: 1.002^300 is about 1.82 and 1.02^30 is about 1.81: a tiny rate over centuries does no more than a modest rate over one generation, which is why England's centuries before 1700 look flat.
